rule: MacroFactor goal per block phase: cut ~0.5% BW/week with high protein; recomp maintenance-to-slight deficit; lean gain ~0.25% BW/week; maintenance fuel-matched to training
summary: The cut rate sits at the conservative end of the bodybuilding consensus range (0.5-1%/week). In an RCT in athletes, ~0.7%/week preserved or added lean mass where 1.4%/week did not. A meta-regression found deficits of about 500 kcal/day stop lean-mass gains, and 0.5% of ~90 kg is roughly that, so 0.5% is the sensible ceiling for a concurrent athlete. Lean gain of 0.25%/week matches the off-season review's 0.25-0.5% (more conservative for advanced lifters), and a 2023 RCT in trained lifters found larger surpluses mostly added fat. Recomp near maintenance fits the finding that a surplus helps but its size is unknown. The numbers come from physique-sport and short trials, not hybrid athletes, so watch them against the EA flag in run-heavy blocks.

sources.note: Helms 2014 contest-prep recommendations: lose ~0.5-1% BW/week to maximise muscle retention
Athletes losing 0.7%/week gained LBM (+2.1%); 1.4%/week did not (-0.2%)
Energy deficit impairs lean-mass gains (ES -0.57) but not strength; ~500 kcal/day deficit prevented LM gains
Off-season review: ~10-20% surplus, target gain 0.25-0.5% BW/week; advanced lifters more conservative
Trained lifters, maintenance vs +5% vs +15% kcal for 8 weeks: faster weight gain mainly increased skinfolds, not muscle thickness
Slater 2019: an energy surplus is anabolic, but the optimal size has never been validated in resistance-trained people

value_at_review.cut: MacroFactor: weight loss ~0.5% BW/week (coached, moderate); protein high
value_at_review.maintenance: MacroFactor: maintenance, fuel-matched to training load
